extra.message: handoff() parses the partner assertion JWT with JWTParser.parse(...).getJWTClaimsSet() and never verifies a signature (no JWSVerifier/MACVerifier call). An attacker can submit any unsigned or arbitrary JWT with any 'sub' claim and receive a valid Northstar session for that user, including admin accounts, achieving full authentication bypass / account takeover.

cwe: CWE-347: Improper Verification of Cryptographic Signature

extra.message: business() uses the caller-supplied 'regionEndpoint' (DecisionResource.kyb passes through the client header X-Core-Region unmodified) directly as the HTTP request base URL with no allowlist. An authenticated underwriter/admin can redirect the server's outbound request, carrying a valid bearer token, to an arbitrary internal or external host (SSRF).

testWebhook() uses the client-supplied X-Callback-Override header as the outbound HTTP POST destination with no validation, unlike webhook creation which enforces a localhost/core-mock allowlist. This lets an admin-level caller make the server issue arbitrary outbound HTTP requests to any host (SSRF).

normaliseScan() builds a shell command string using the raw value of the client-controlled NS_SCAN_GEOMETRY cookie ('size') and executes it via new ProcessBuilder("sh","-c",command). A cookie value such as '100x100; rm -rf /' (or any shell metacharacters) is executed on the server. This is OS command injection reachable from the authenticated document-upload endpoint.

The /admin/webhooks endpoint parses input.formatSpec() with an ObjectMapper configured via activateDefaultTyping(LaissezFaireSubTypeValidator.instance, NON_FINAL). LaissezFaireSubTypeValidator permits deserializing arbitrary classes named in the JSON, which is a classic gadget-chain RCE vector for Jackson polymorphic deserialization.

importLeads() builds a native SQL query by directly concatenating c[2].trim() (the 'business_name' field parsed from the uploaded CSV) into the query string: "select count(*) from borrower_lead where business_name = '" + c[2].trim() + "'". A business name containing a single quote breaks out of the string literal, enabling SQL injection, in contrast to every other query in this file which correctly uses bound parameters.

quote() evaluates the stored product.rateExpression string (settable via /admin/products' rateExpression field) with ognl.Ognl.getValue() against a context that is directly reachable from any authenticated caller of /products/{id}/quote. OGNL expression evaluation of attacker-influenceable strings is a well-known code-execution vector (OGNL injection); any compromised/malicious admin-level input results in arbitrary server-side code execution on every quote request.

cwe: CWE-917: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an Expression Language Statement

extra.message: statement() builds an XPath expression by concatenating the client-supplied NS_STMT_FILTER cookie directly into "//balance[account='" + filter + "']" and evaluates it against the core-fetched statement XML. An attacker can inject XPath syntax (e.g. ' or '1'='1) to alter the query logic and extract balance data beyond what the filter was meant to permit.

cwe: CWE-643: Improper Neutralization of Data within XPath Expressions

extra.message: resolve() builds the LDAP search filter by directly concatenating the caller-supplied 'principal' value: "(&(objectClass=person)(uid=" + principal + "))" with no escaping of LDAP filter metacharacters (e.g. '*', '(', ')'). A crafted principal can alter the filter logic to broaden or bypass the intended search (LDAP injection).

cwe: CWE-90: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an LDAP Query

extra.message: upload() looks up the LoanDocument by raw id via LoanDocument.findById(id) — skipping the access.document(actor,id) ownership/scope check entirely — whenever the caller's role is support_specialist and the client sends any non-blank X-Support-Branch header. The header value is never validated against the actor's actual branch/queue, so any support_specialist can upload (and tamper with) documents belonging to any application in the system by id, bypassing the application-scope access control that protects every other endpoint.

cwe: CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key

extra.message: brandingLogo() resolves the stored file path as brandStore.resolve(logo.fileName()) using the raw, attacker-controlled multipart filename, with no .normalize() + startsWith(base) containment check (unlike the sibling document upload/download handlers in the same class, which do perform this check). A filename like '../../../../opt/app/something' lets an admin-level caller write a file outside the branding directory.

notice() takes the raw value of the client-controlled NS_NOTICE_TEMPLATE cookie and passes it as the Velocity template source into noticeRenderer.render(template, ...), which calls Velocity.evaluate(context, writer, name, source) (NoticeRenderer.java:15). Velocity templates can invoke arbitrary Java methods via $class.inspect / context object traversal, so an attacker-controlled template string leads to server-side template injection and remote code execution.

cwe: CWE-1336: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements Used in a Template Engine

extra.message: summary() concatenates the raw @QueryParam('caption') value, and the businessName/reference/requestedAmount/currency fields, directly into a hand-built HTML string returned as text/html with no escaping. A URL such as /applications/1/summary?caption=<script>...</script> reflects attacker script into the authenticated page.

The filter reflects the request's Origin header verbatim into Access-Control-Allow-Origin and also sets Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true for the dashboard/applications/documents paths. This permits any arbitrary origin to make credentialed cross-origin requests and read the authenticated response (borrower PII, loan/document data), defeating same-origin protections for these sensitive endpoints.

cwe: CWE-942: Permissive Cross-domain Policy with Untrusted Domains

extra.message: X-Frame-Options: DENY is stripped from any HTML response whenever the request carries a cookie named NS_PARTNER_VIEW with any value. Since cookies are set purely client-side (e.g. via a malicious page on a related origin or by the attacker instructing the victim), an attacker can set this cookie in the victim's browser and then frame authenticated pages (dashboard, applications, documents) for clickjacking.

cwe: CWE-1021: Improper Restriction of Rendered UI Layers or Frames

extra.message: openStatement() decrypts the client-supplied 'seal' with AES/CBC/PKCS5Padding (StatementCipher.open) and returns a distinct HTTP status (403) for BadPaddingException versus a different status (400) for other GeneralSecurityException/IllegalArgumentException failures. This observable discrepancy between a padding failure and any other failure is the classic oracle needed to mount a Vaudenay padding-oracle attack and decrypt or forge ciphertext without the key.

referral() decrypts the client-supplied 'envelope' form field with AES/CBC/PKCS5Padding (EnvelopeCodec.open) and returns a different HTTP status/message for BadPaddingException (400) versus other GeneralSecurityException/IllegalArgumentException failures (422). This distinguishable failure behavior is a padding-oracle side channel that allows decrypting/forging the ciphertext without knowledge of the key.

A fixed admin-role account (auditor@northstar.local) is provisioned on every startup using the hardcoded literal password "Northstar#Audit2026". Anyone with access to the source (or this value) can log in as an admin on any deployment that hasn't separately rotated this credential.

provisionConsole() stores the legacy console passphrase hashed with DigestUtils.md5Hex() and accessConsole() (lines 1323-1324) compares against the same MD5 hash, unlike every other credential in the app which uses BcryptUtil.bcryptHash (see AuthLifecycleResource). MD5 is fast and unsalted, making these passphrases practical to crack offline if the password table is exposed.

cwe: CWE-916: Use of Password Hash With Insufficient Computational Effort
CWE-327: Use of a Broken or Risky Cryptographic Algorithm

extra.message: userDetail() includes the raw stored password hash (u.passwordHash) in the JSON response under 'credentialRecord'. Returning password hashes to any client response (even to an admin UI) unnecessarily exposes material that can be cracked or replayed if the response is logged, cached, or intercepted.

cwe: CWE-200: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor

extra.message: The DSESSION session cookie is built with .secure(false), so it can be transmitted over plain HTTP, and its SameSite policy is downgraded from STRICT to NONE whenever the client sends an X-Legacy-Client header — a value the client fully controls. NONE plus a non-Secure cookie weakens both transport confidentiality and CSRF protections for the session token.

cwe: CWE-1275: Sensitive Cookie with Improper SameSite Attribute

extra.message: read() takes the 'account' attribute parsed from the uploaded transaction XML and concatenates it unescaped into an XPath expression: "//transaction[account='" + account + "']". An uploaded feed with an 'account' value containing XPath metacharacters alters the query's matching logic (XPath injection).

cwe: CWE-643: Improper Neutralization of Data within XPath Expressions

extra.message: revenueReport() builds the outbound request URL by directly concatenating the caller-supplied 'account' query parameter (and 'reference') into the query string after the internal apiKey parameter, with no URL-encoding: "...?apiKey=" + key + "&account=" + account + "&reference=" + reference. An account value containing '&' lets an authenticated underwriter/admin inject or override additional query parameters sent to the internal revenue-gateway service.

availability() returns the explicit message "This email is already registered." vs "This email is available to register." whenever the client sends X-App-Channel: legacy — an attacker-controlled header — letting anyone enumerate registered email addresses on the platform.

noteFailure() writes the raw, unsanitized user-submitted email address into the application log via ONBOARDING_LOG.warnf. An email value containing newline/control characters can forge additional log lines (log injection).

cwe: CWE-117: Improper Output Neutralization for Logs
